newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close modestly higher on high techs.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close modestly higher on high techs.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed modestly higher on Thursday, as high technology shares were bought following a record winning streak in technology stocks on Wall Street, brokers said.

But the rally was capped by concern over the financial health of some firms and the decision on which penalties will be recommended for Nomura Securities Co Ltd. The penalties are likely to be announced as early as next week.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 57.61 points or 0.29 percent to close at 19,754.78. It briefly touched 19,820.58.
September Nikkei futures ended 80 points higher at 19,780.

"The market was split into two," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd. "While high-tech shares were strong, shares in some financially weak firms were sold, following the news of Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd," he said.
Last Friday, Tokai Kogyo said it had filed for court

Brokers said foreign investors stepped up buying of high-tech issues. "The Dow industrials fell overnight but Nasdaq (technical shares) rose and prompted buying in Japanese high-tech issues," a trader at a foreign brokerage said. The Nasdaq composite index on Wednesday rose 1.53 points to

But strategists said high-tech sector's upturn was not expected to spark a strong, broad rally in Tokyo stocks. "Buying was limited to high-tech shares," said Ken Okamura, strategist at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson (Asia) Ltd.

"High-tech firms were bought, but given the level of the yen, they are not likely to make as much profits (in the latter half of 1997/98) as they are forecast to in the first half of this financial year," he said.

Brokers said the market was somewhat quiet ahead of the July options settlement on Friday. Investors were also sidelined awaiting Japan's securities watchdog to make recommendations to the finance minister on penalties on Nomura, which has been linked to a corporate racketeer scandal. Financial markets are speculating that the Finance Ministry may suspend part of Nomura's business for up to six months. On the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, turnover was 352 million shares on Thursday, against 355 million shares on Wednesday. Gainers marginally outpaced losers 519 to 507, while 201 issues were unchanged.

The broader TOPIX index added 4.59 points or 0.31 percent to end at 1,499.11. The Nikkei 300 average firmed 0.75 point or 0.26 percent to 290.42. Major computer maker Fujitsu Ltd was the most heavily traded issue with 9.539 million shares changing hands. The shares jumped 50 yen to close at 1,610. Another computer firm NEC Corp gained 20 yen to close at 1,590. It was the eighth-most heavily traded issue with turnover of 4.221 million shares. Yaohan Japan Corp shares remained under pressure due to persistent anxiety over its financial health. Traders said the supermarket chain operator struggles with heavy debt after aggressive expansion overseas.
Yaohan fell 17 yen or 10.63 percent to end at 143, the
largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

Yaohan on Thursday said it was not considering applying to the court for an arrangement with creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws. He also said that financial institutions remain supportive of Yaohan's restructuring efforts.

General contractor Aoki Corp, also hurt by worries over its financial health, finished six yen lower at 100. Isuzu Motors Ltd jumped on news that the car maker and General Motors Corp of the United States were considering transferring GM's diesel engine development and production to Isuzu. The shares rose 48 yen to end at 435. Nintendo Co Ltd's shares gained, fuelled by
robust sales of its new game software in the United States, to finish 400 yen higher at 9,700.

The second section index rose 9.72 points to 1,811.28, with 9.48 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 0.57 point at 1,186.90. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
